Treatment-by-mediator interaction

Source: vignettes/articles/model-interaction.qmd

When the effect of the mediator depends on the treatment, the outcome model carries a treatment * mediator term and the effect splits into four parts. Part of the Models collection.

Structure X to M to Y, with an X by M term in the outcome model
Class returned InteractionMediationData
Routes fit_mediation() (glm or regmedint engine), extract_mediation() on lm/glm or lavaan
Needs Gaussian identity-link models and a reference mediator level m_star 
library(medfit)

Attaching package: 'medfit'
The following object is masked from 'package:stats':

    decompose
library(generics)

Attaching package: 'generics'
The following objects are masked from 'package:base':

    as.difftime, as.factor, as.ordered, intersect, is.element, setdiff,
    setequal, union

Fit it

Write the product in the outcome formula; medfit recognizes it and returns the four-way class. m_star is the mediator level at which the controlled direct effect is evaluated (default 0).

fit <- fit_mediation(
  outcome_int ~ treatment * mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
  mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2,
  data = mediation_demo, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
  m_star = 0
)
class(fit)[1]
[1] "medfit::InteractionMediationData"
decompose(fit)
       cde    int_ref    int_med        pie        nde        nie      total
0.21521278 0.04353909 0.27709549 0.34001758 0.25875187 0.61711307 0.87586495

The four parts

Part Name Reads as
cde controlled direct effect effect of the treatment with the mediator held at m_star
int_ref reference interaction interaction due to the mediator’s level without the treatment
int_med mediated interaction interaction that operates through the treatment’s effect on the mediator
pie pure indirect effect effect through the mediator with no interaction 
parts <- decompose(fit)
c(nde = unname(parts["cde"] + parts["int_ref"]),
  nie = unname(parts["int_med"] + parts["pie"]),
  total = unname(sum(parts[c("cde", "int_ref", "int_med", "pie")])))
      nde       nie     total
0.2587519 0.6171131 0.8758649

The natural direct effect is cde + int_ref, the natural indirect effect is int_med + pie, and the four add to the total effect.

Same result from the closed-form engine

engine = "regmedint" computes the same quantities from the closed-form regression formulas, with analytical standard errors (needs the suggested regmedint package).

fit_rm <- fit_mediation(
  outcome_int ~ treatment * mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
  mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2,
  data = mediation_demo, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
  engine = "regmedint"
)
all.equal(decompose(fit_rm), decompose(fit))
[1] TRUE

Limits

  • Only products written with : or * in the outcome model are recognized. A product precomputed as a data column cannot be seen and would be ignored, so write it in the formula.
  • Non-Gaussian outcomes or mediators error; see glm families for what is supported there.
  • The native engine does not support the four-way decomposition (it estimates no mediator intercept).
